outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the best known upper exponent for the wasted space W(x) has moved from 5/8 to 3/5, through two independent constructions (McClenagan, MSc thesis dated August 2024 and arXiv 1 February 2026; Bui, arXiv 6 August 2025, revised 15 March 2026), while the lower exponent 1/2 (Roth–Vaughan, 1978) and the exact asymptotic rate are unchanged and still open; the 2019 Chung–Graham proof of the same 3/5 bound has been reported erroneous.
problem_asks: (1) The asymptotic growth rate, as the side x tends to infinity, of W(x): the least area left uncovered when non-overlapping unit squares are packed into a square of side x (W(x) = x² minus the largest number of unit squares that fit). The question asks for the rate itself, i.e. a matching order or exponent, which requires both an upper bound (a family of packings) and a lower bound (every packing wastes at least this much). (2) The bullet does not restrict x to any class of side lengths. The Wikipedia article's unsolved-problem template and its text phrase the open question for half-integer side lengths ('even for half-integer side lengths'); that restriction is Wikipedia's wording, not the bullet's, and it is recorded here so the judging pass can see both. Nothing else is asked.

events.what_happened: Erdős and Graham, 'On packing squares with equal squares', Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A) 19 (1975) 119–123 (volume and pages as printed in Bui's bibliography, arXiv:2508.04603v2). Explicit packings of unit squares in a square of side a, tilting some squares, leave uncovered area O(a^{7/11}); axis-parallel packings waste order a·{a}. Pre-window; recorded because it is the first bound and the baseline for every later event. I could not read the PDF (binary response), so the content is taken from Friedman's survey and Bui's text.
events.delivers: Upper bound W(a) = O(a^{7/11}) for all a. No restriction on side lengths.
events.remains: The exact order; any matching lower bound.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A), refereed journal of record
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record in combinatorics
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the note (journal acceptance; no separate verification record)

events.direction: Upper bound on W. No conjectured rate is stated, so it neither confirms nor refutes one.
events.object: Explicit construction (tilted packings of unit squares in a square of side a) giving uncovered area O(a^{7/11}). Constructive, not an existence proof.

events.what_happened: Roth and Vaughan, 'Inefficiency in packing squares with unit squares', Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A) 24(2) (1978) 170–186 (per Bui's bibliography and the Wikipedia reference). Lower bound on wasted space. As printed in Friedman's survey text (extraction garbled, so check the original): if s(s−⌊s⌋) > 1/6 then W(s) ≥ 10^{-100}·√(s·|s−⌊s+½⌋|). For half-integer s this is of order √s, so W is not o(s^{1/2}) and not O(s^α) for α < 1/2.
events.delivers: Lower bound W(s) ≥ c·√s (c = 10^{-100}) for half-integer s, with the fractional-part condition as the survey prints it. Establishes that the exponent is at least 1/2.
events.remains: The exact exponent between 1/2 and the upper bound; for the rate question, the whole gap above 1/2.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A), refereed journal of record
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record in combinatorics
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper; restated in Friedman's survey and Bui's introduction

events.doubts: The exact condition on the fractional part is garbled in the survey text I could read, and several secondary summaries write the bound as 10^{-100}√(x−⌊x⌋), which is not the survey's form. The judging pass should check the original before relying on the half-integer statement.
events.direction: Lower bound. It is the half of the rate question that bounds from below; it does not conflict with any upper bound.

events.what_happened: Chung and Graham, Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A) 116(6) (2009) 1167–1175 (per Bui's bibliography). Upper bound W(x) = O(x^{(3+√2)/7} log x), exponent about 0.631.
events.delivers: Upper bound with exponent (3+√2)/7 and a log factor, for all x.
events.remains: The exact order; the lower exponent 1/2.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A), refereed journal of record

events.direction: Upper bound. Improves on 7/11 and is superseded by Wang–Dong–Li's 5/8 in 2016.
events.object: Explicit packing construction (recursive, trapezoid-based per Bui's description). Constructive, not an object.

events.what_happened: Shuang Wang, Tian Dong and Jiamin Li (Jilin University), 'A New Result on Packing Unit Squares into a Large Square', arXiv:1603.02368, submitted 8 March 2016, revised 9 April 2016. Improves the uncovered-area bound to O(x^{5/8}) (exponent 0.625) and the dual covering bound to x² + O(x^{5/8}). I found no journal version in my searches (a search summary says the manuscript targets JCTA; not confirmed).
events.delivers: Upper bound W(x) = O(x^{5/8}) for all x. Also improves the covering dual.
events.remains: The exact order; the lower exponent 1/2.
events.direction: Upper bound. Improves on Chung–Graham 2009 and is the best refereed-era exponent that later events improve on.

events.what_happened: Fan Chung and Ron Graham, 'Efficient packings of unit squares in a large square', Discrete & Computational Geometry 64(3) (690–699), listed as 2019 in Bui's bibliography and in secondary sources (McClenagan's preprint cites 2020; volume 64 is the 2020 volume). The note states that the uncovered area W(x) 'can be made as small as O(x^{3/5})', improving the 2009 bound. The publisher page was not reachable; the wording comes from a search excerpt of the UCSD preprint. The UCSD PDF itself is not readable in my tool.
events.revisions: Preprint on R. Graham's UCSD page is undated (not read). Journal version as above; McClenagan's preprint gives 2020 for the claim.
events.delivers: Claimed upper bound W(x) = O(x^{3/5}) for all x, by a proof that later sources report to contain an error.
events.remains: The exact order. The 3/5 claim is disputed (see doubts).

checked_by.who: Discrete & Computational Geometry, refereed journal of record
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record in computational geometry
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the note (journal acceptance). Acceptance is weak evidence here, since later sources report an error in its argument.

events.doubts: Two sources say the argument for 3/5 is wrong. (1) Arslanov and Bui (DCG, 2025), as cited in Bui's arXiv:2508.04603v1 and v2 introduction: 'shows that there is a technical error in the calculation of W5'. I could not open that note. (2) McClenagan's MSc thesis (August 2024) states 'we found that their proof contains an error'. McClenagan's 2026 preprint, by contrast, says the bound claimed here is in fact correct, using a new algorithm. So the exponent 3/5 has been claimed correct and the 2019 proof has been flagged erroneous; the two are not in conflict as stated, but the record has no published repair of the 2019 argument.
events.direction: Claims the 3/5 exponent. That exponent is the upper bound the question's rate would be measured against; the claim is an upper bound, not a resolution of the rate.
events.object: Explicit packing construction. No single object.

events.what_happened: Montgomery is reported in Friedman's survey (2009 version opened) as improving the Erdős–Graham bound to O(s^{(3−√3)/2+ε}), exponent about 0.634, by personal communication. No written proof was located. Friedman's survey carries a corrigendum dated 1 March 2023 on this exponent (per the survey text I read; its content not seen). The same exponent is cited as 'personal communication' in McClenagan's 2026 preprint and in Wikipedia.
events.revisions: Friedman survey corrigendum 1 March 2023 (per the survey text read; not verified).
events.delivers: Claimed upper bound with exponent (3−√3)/2 ≈ 0.634 (+ε), if the personal communication holds.
events.remains: The exact order; the lower exponent 1/2.
events.doubts: No written proof exists in the sources I read; the exponent rests on personal communication. It is weaker than Wang–Dong–Li's 5/8 (since 0.634 > 0.625) and so was superseded in 2016. The date is the survey version I opened; the bound may be older.
people: Montgomery (first name not given in sources)

events.what_happened: Rory McClenagan, MSc thesis 'Asymptotic Square Packing Problems', University of Northern British Columbia, dated August 2024 (UNBC repository folder 2024-09). Its second result: the wasted space when packing a square of side x by unit squares is O(x^{3/5}) (Theorem 1.2, ch. 1; restated in ch. 5). The thesis also says the Chung–Graham proof of this bound 'contains an error'. The same mathematics was posted to arXiv as 2602.01484 on 1 February 2026 (one version listed); that preprint says it was extracted from the 2024 thesis, and states 'the bound claimed by Chung and Graham in [1] is, in fact, correct, using a new algorithm'. Its main theorem is 'Theorem 1. The wasted space in packing the square S(x) by unit squares is bounded by W(x) = O(x^{3/5}).' The thesis's first result (a multidimensional generalisation of a Tao result on the Meir–Moser problem) is a different problem.
events.revisions: UNBC repository posting (folder dated 2024-09). arXiv:2602.01484 v1, 1 Feb 2026, the only version listed. The preprint's title page, as the text extraction reads it, says 'August 24, 2026', which does not match its arXiv stamp; I could not reconcile this.
events.delivers: W(x) = O(x^{3/5}) for all large x, with no log factor and no half-integer restriction, by an explicit packing algorithm (stacks of unit squares, leftover right trapezoids handled by two sub-algorithms, then optimised parameters). An upper bound on W with exponent 3/5. It gives no lower bound beyond 1/2 and no exact rate.
events.remains: The exact asymptotic order; the gap between the lower exponent 1/2 (Roth–Vaughan) and the upper exponent 3/5; the half-integer version is not separately settled.

checked_by.qualification: Named as the thesis supervisor and as a proofreader of the 2026 preprint (supervisor listing from a search summary of the UNBC record; proofreading from the preprint's acknowledgements, which I read)
checked_by.what_they_did: Supervised the MSc thesis; proofread the arXiv preprint. Not a stated independent verification of the proof.

checked_by.qualification: Author of an independent O(x^{3/5}) construction (arXiv:2508.04603)
checked_by.what_they_did: Compares the two methods in arXiv:2508.04603v2 §1.1: says McClenagan's second algorithm is a special case of Bui's (Δ₁+Δ₂=1) and that McClenagan's right-trapezoid method is 'completely different'. No verification of the proof is claimed.

events.time_since_posted: 26 months since the thesis (Aug 2024); 8 months since the arXiv posting (Feb 2026)
events.directly_checkable: The construction is an explicit algorithm for each side length x; a reader can run it for a given x and count the uncovered area. No computation by anyone is reported in the sources.
events.doubts: (1) Single author; an unrefereed MSc thesis and an arXiv preprint with no journal venue in the record. (2) The thesis says Chung–Graham's proof of this bound is erroneous; the 2026 preprint says the bound itself is correct via a new algorithm. Both are the author's statements and are not reconciled in the sources I read. (3) No third-party verification of either document found. (4) The preprint's title-page date does not match its arXiv stamp (see revisions). Nothing in the sources says the thesis or preprint was withdrawn or corrected.
events.direction: Upper bound with exponent 3/5, improving the 5/8 bound of 2016. It does not touch the lower exponent or the exact rate, so it neither settles the rate nor cuts against any stated conjecture.
events.object: An explicit packing of unit squares in a square of side x, for each x, with uncovered area O(x^{3/5}). It is constructed by an algorithm (described in the abstract and the thesis), not by existence. The construction is the object; the sources give no computed instance.

events.what_happened: Hong Duc Bui, 'Square Packing with Asymptotically Smallest Waste Only Needs Good Squares', arXiv:2504.09489 (cs.CG), submitted 13 April 2025, one version. Comments: 'submitted to CCCG 2025'. Theorem 1.1: W(x) ∈ Θ(W*(x)), where W* is the minimum waste over packings using only good squares (tilt at most 10^{-10}); Proposition 3 gives W*(x) ≤ c₂·W(x). It uses this to simplify the Roth–Vaughan lower-bound argument. No new exponent is claimed.
events.delivers: A reduction for the asymptotic question: the minimum waste is equivalent, up to a constant, to the minimum over packings of good squares only. It simplifies the proof of W ∉ o(x^{1/2}). It holds for all x. It moves no exponent.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: the lower exponent 1/2 is unchanged, the upper exponent is unchanged by this paper, and the exact rate is open.
events.direction: Neutral to the exponents: a reduction lemma that bears on the lower-bound proof, cutting neither toward nor away from any rate.

events.what_happened: Marat Arslanov and Hong Duc Bui, a note on Chung and Graham's 'Efficient packings of unit squares in a large square', listed as Discrete & Computational Geometry (2025) in Bui's bibliography. Per Bui's introduction it 'shows that there is a technical error in the calculation of W5' in the 2019 argument. I could not locate the note in search or open it. A search summary gives August 2025; I could not verify that date.
events.delivers: Per Bui's description only: a technical error in the W5 computation of Chung–Graham's argument. Sets no bound on W.
events.remains: Nothing from this event on the bound; its effect is on whether the 2019 proof of 3/5 stands.

checked_by.who: Marat Arslanov and Hong Duc Bui (authors)
checked_by.qualification: Not established from the sources I could read
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a note identifying an error in the 2019 argument (per Bui's citation). I did not read the note.

events.time_since_posted: about 1 year if the 2025 date is right
events.doubts: The note's existence, venue and content rest on Bui's citation alone; I could not open it. Bui is a co-author and also the author of the competing 3/5 construction, a conflict the judging pass should weigh. McClenagan's preprint does not mention this note.
events.direction: Against the correctness of Chung–Graham's 2019 proof of 3/5. Neutral on whether 3/5 is true.

events.what_happened: Hong Duc Bui, 'Square packing with O(x^{0.6}) wasted area', arXiv:2508.04603, single author, v1 submitted 6 August 2025 (24 pages, 20 figures). Abstract: 'We show a new construction for square packing, and prove that it is more efficient than previous results.' Main theorem: W(x) ∈ O(x^{3/5}) (Theorem 5.14 in v1, Theorem 5.20 in v2), from a general family W_{β,ε}(x) = x^{2β/(2β+1)} log^{ε/(2β+1)} x with β = 3/4. v2 (15 March 2026) cites McClenagan, states the Arslanov–Bui error, and adds sharper-exponent conjectures (Conjectures 6.21–6.22, Question 6.23).
events.revisions: v1 6 Aug 2025 (Theorem 5.14; no mention of McClenagan). v2 15 Mar 2026 (Theorem 5.20; cites McClenagan's thesis and preprint; states that McClenagan's result was 'independently discovered'; thanks 'anonymous reviewers'). Same claim in both versions.
events.delivers: W(x) ∈ O(x^{3/5}) for all x, with no half-integer restriction, via a new explicit construction. Improves 5/8. Gives no lower bound beyond 1/2.
events.remains: The exact asymptotic order; the gap between the lower exponent 1/2 and the upper exponent 3/5. The paper's own conjectures for sharper exponents (6.21–6.22) and Question 6.23 (whether o(x^{3/5}) is possible when the fractional part of x is Θ(x^{-2/5})) remain open.

checked_by.who: Anonymous referees (thanked in v2's acknowledgements; venue not named)
checked_by.what_they_did: Unknown. v2 thanks them 'for many helpful suggestions to improve the manuscript'.

checked_by.qualification: Author of an independent O(x^{3/5}) result (thesis August 2024)
checked_by.what_they_did: Mentions the paper in the comments and text of arXiv:2602.01484 as 'a similar result by a different method'. No verification of the proof is claimed.

events.directly_checkable: The construction is explicit for each x. No computational check is reported in the sources.
events.doubts: (1) The exponent is the same as the 2019 Chung–Graham claim whose argument is reported erroneous; Bui's paper is a new construction rather than a repair of that argument, and I found no public verification of it. (2) No venue is named, and the referees are thanked but unnamed. (3) Priority: v2 says McClenagan's result was 'independently discovered', but McClenagan's thesis predates this v1 by a year (see disputes). No scope change between v1 and v2 (both state O(x^{3/5})).
events.direction: Upper bound: improves the exponent to 3/5. Neither for nor against any stated conjecture, since the question asks for the rate.
events.object: An explicit packing family: for each large x, a packing of unit squares in a square of side x with uncovered area O(x^{3/5}), from a new construction (described in §5, which the summarising fetch did not reproduce in full). Constructive, not an existence proof.

events.what_happened: Optimal side length for 11 unit squares, s(11) ≈ 3.8770836, the value of Walter Trump's 1979 packing. Ahmed (X handle @ManassehA06, given as 'Mannaseh Ahmed' in some secondary coverage) published a proof dated 'Original proof September 29, 2026' (Squares Project review; Wikipedia: 'shown on September 29, 2026 in an AI-assisted proof'). The optimality certificate is in Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresOptimal, whose README calls it 'a computer-assisted certificate proof', says 'It is not a completed Lean/formal proof', and says 'publication here does not constitute independent peer review'. A Lean 4 formalisation, Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized, was announced 6 October 2026. This is a different quantity (the smallest square holding exactly 11 squares), not the asymptotic waste. Discarded for scope; recorded because it is the AI-related result on this topic that is most visible.
events.revisions: Squares Project exposition first published 30 Sep 2026. Lean formalisation announced 6 Oct 2026 (aiweekly; README links docs/VERIFICATION_20261006.md). Earlier Lean drafts reportedly had six sorry placeholders (secondary reports).
events.delivers: Settles the optimal side for one finite case, n = 11 (s(11) equals Trump's 1979 value). Nothing about W(x) as x grows.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the asymptotic rate of wasted space.

checked_by.qualification: Maintainer of the public project; the review page is written by the project
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a review of the optimality proof; states that verification and confirmation reviews 'remain pending on both axes' and that the project 'has replayed neither proof in full'

checked_by.who: GPT-6 Pro (as named on the review page)
checked_by.qualification: AI model used as an adversarial reviewer
checked_by.what_they_did: Recomputed the exposition's numbers and reported 'no mathematical error' (review page wording). Reviewed the exposition, not the proof.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (formalisation), with native_decide and the native compiler trusted

events.directly_checkable: One explicit arrangement of eleven unit squares (Trump 1979) in a square of side ≈ 3.8770836; the numerical certificates are in the repositories.
events.doubts: (1) The README states that the complete optimality proof 'passed verification with native numerical certificates' and that the final theorem trusts 'Lean's kernel and native compiler; this is not a kernel-only verification claim'. (2) The optimality repository says it is not a completed Lean proof and is not peer-reviewed. (3) The sorry_free value rests on secondary reports ('zero admissions'); I did not confirm it in the repository. (4) Sources disagree on which AI systems contributed (see disputes).
events.direction: Confirms a known packing is optimal for n = 11, if the proof stands. Neutral to the asymptotic question.
events.object: Trump's 1979 packing of eleven unit squares in a square of side ≈ 3.8770836, shown optimal by a certificate-based argument (not existence).

systems.name: GPT-6 Astra
systems.what_it_did: Listed as an 'Agent' on the review page. The review says 'Ahmed's announcement credits Astra's work building on the Squares Project and Kleddamag'. The case page describes the proof as 'Astra-assisted work building on Squares Project and Kleddamag' (there it is named 'Astra'). The sources say nothing about what Astra contributed to the mathematics. The Squares Project relays Ahmed's announcement; I did not open Ahmed's X post.

events.what_happened: Jineon Baek, Junnosuke Koizumi and Takahiro Ueoro, 'A note on the Erdős conjecture about square packing', arXiv:2411.07274 (v1 11 Nov 2024; v2 18 Nov 2024; RIKEN-iTHEMS-Report-24). Defines f(n) as the maximum total side length of n squares packed in a unit square. Proves Erdős's conjecture f(k²+1) = k under the added assumption that all squares are axis-parallel (g(k²+2c+1) = k + c/k). The general conjecture is listed as open on erdosproblems.com #106. This is a different quantity from wasted space: a neighbouring problem in the same literature, discarded for scope.
events.delivers: The axis-parallel case of the Erdős sum-of-side-lengths conjecture, f(k²+1) = k restricted to axis-parallel squares. Says nothing about W(x).
events.remains: The unrestricted sum-of-sides conjecture, and everything in problem_asks.
events.direction: Different problem (sum of side lengths, not uncovered area). Neutral to the asymptotic question.

events.what_happened: Anshul Raj Singh, 'On a square packing conjecture of Erdős', arXiv:2601.22163, submitted 10 January 2026. Shows that Erdős's conjecture f(k²+1) = k (sum of side lengths) is equivalent to convergence of Σ(f(k²+1) − k), and compares the square and triangle cases. A different problem from wasted space, discarded for scope.
events.delivers: Equivalence of the sum-of-side-lengths conjecture with a series convergence. Says nothing about W(x).
events.direction: Different problem. Neutral to the asymptotic question.

events.what_happened: Samuel Korsky, 'Approximating 1 by Sums of Unit Fractions', arXiv:2607.04157, v1 5 July 2026, v2 8 October 2026. Improves an Erdős–Graham bound on unit fractions. A namesake only: it has nothing to do with packing squares. A search snippet had linked it to GPT-5.5 Pro; the abstract page I opened has no acknowledgement or AI credit.
events.delivers: A bound on unit-fraction sums. Namesake only.
events.direction: Different problem sharing a namesake. Neutral.

disputes.summary: Independent O(x^{3/5}) constructions. McClenagan's MSc thesis (August 2024; arXiv 1 February 2026) and Bui's arXiv preprint (6 August 2025; v2 15 March 2026) both claim W(x) = O(x^{3/5}) by new constructions. Bui's v2 says 'an equivalent result was independently discovered by McClenagan' and that McClenagan's second algorithm is a special case of Bui's construction while the right-trapezoid method is 'completely different'. The thesis predates Bui's preprint by a year, and Bui cites it. Whether this priority matters is for the judging pass; the dates are recorded above.

The 2019 Chung–Graham proof of W(x) = O(x^{3/5}). Arslanov and Bui (DCG 2025, as cited by Bui; not opened) say it has a technical error in the W5 calculation. McClenagan's thesis says 'their proof contains an error'. McClenagan's 2026 preprint says the bound is 'in fact, correct, using a new algorithm'. The sources agree on the exponent only through the two new constructions, not through the 2019 argument, which has no published repair in the record.

Which AI systems contributed to the 11-square optimality result (a result on s(11), not the asymptotic question). The Squares Project review says the Lean work is not attributed to any named AI system and credits wand125 and Ahmed. The case page quotes Ahmed's X post as 'formalized in lean thanks to Astra and Claude'. aiweekly says the Lean repository 'names two AI systems, OpenAI's Astra and Anthropic's Claude, as direct contributors'. The fetched 11SquaresFormalized README names no AI system. Wikipedia says only 'an AI-assisted proof'. Secondary headlines also use 'GPT-6 Astra' and 'Astra 6'. The record uses only the strings the review page gives; Claude is not entered in ai.systems because its only credited role is formalisation.

Wikipedia's open-problem template and text frame the rate question for half-integer side lengths ('even for half-integer side lengths'). The bullet's statement asks for the asymptotic growth rate without that restriction. The Roth–Vaughan lower bound is stated for half-integers in Wikipedia and in Bui's text, and as 10^{-100}√(s·|s−⌊s+½⌋|) in Friedman's survey. The upper bounds in this record hold for all x.

summary: Thirty-seven web searches and about twenty-five opened pages (most read through a summarising fetcher; see incomplete) found no AI involvement in the asymptotic wasted-space problem, and no event that settles the rate. The live development is in the exponent of the upper bound. Wang–Dong–Li's 2016 5/8 was the best exponent in the record until two independent constructions for 3/5 appeared: McClenagan's MSc thesis (UNBC, August 2024, repository posting September 2024; arXiv 2602.01484, 1 February 2026) and Bui's arXiv:2508.04603 (6 August 2025; v2 15 March 2026). I date McClenagan's result to the thesis, as the first public written argument (§5.1); the 2026 arXiv posting is the same mathematics. Both are single-author, unrefereed in the record, and neither has a public third-party verification; they cite each other, and Bui's v2 compares the two methods without claiming to verify the other's proof. The 3/5 exponent was first claimed by Chung and Graham (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2019). Arslanov and Bui (DCG 2025, cited by Bui; I could not open it) say that argument has a technical error in the W5 calculation, and McClenagan's thesis says the same. McClenagan's 2026 preprint says the bound is nonetheless correct, by a new algorithm. Bui's April 2025 preprint (arXiv:2504.09489) reduces the asymptotic question to packings of good squares, simplifying the Roth–Vaughan lower-bound proof without changing its exponent. The lower exponent 1/2 (Roth–Vaughan, 1978) is unchanged, and Wikipedia still calls the exact rate open, framing it for half-integer side lengths. Close calls: (a) dating McClenagan's result to August 2024 rather than February 2026; (b) excluding the AI-assisted 11-square optimality result (29 September 2026, Lean formalisation 6 October 2026) as a different quantity, s(11), rather than as AI involvement in this problem; the wording of its AI attribution varies across sources (see disputes), and I entered only 'GPT-6 Astra', whose only role is described as 'Astra-assisted work', while Claude's credited role is formalisation; (c) the Arslanov–Bui note, recorded from Bui's citation alone. Neighbouring work discarded for scope: Baek–Koizumi–Ueoro (2024) and Raj Singh (2026) on Erdős's sum-of-side-lengths problem; Korsky (2026) on Erdős–Graham unit fractions (a namesake). OpenAI's ten Astra results (1 August 2026) include no square-packing item, per the TheNextWeb article. OpenAI's May 2026 unit-distance result (Erdős #90) is a different problem and I did not open it. The Wikipedia AI sentence is quoted from the page's wikitext. Dataset-level and judging questions are left to the later pass.
competing_reading: Read the asymptotic result as a dispute rather than an improvement. The 3/5 exponent was first claimed in 2019, and the argument for it has been reported erroneous; the two post-2024 constructions are unrefereed, single-author works, and McClenagan's own thesis and preprint give different verdicts on the 2019 argument. On this reading the best refereed upper bound is still 5/8 (Wang–Dong–Li, 2016), or (3+√2)/7 with a log factor (Chung–Graham, 2009) if one counts only the journal-level record without the 2019 claim, and no refereed bound moved in the window. The opposite reading is that two independent constructions reaching the same exponent by different methods is strong evidence for 3/5, since neither depends on the 2019 argument. The record supports both; the difference is whether one counts unrefereed constructions as events that moved the bound.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A refereed or otherwise checked version of either Bui's arXiv:2508.04603 or McClenagan's arXiv:2602.01484 (or the thesis), or a verification note from a third party. (2) The Arslanov–Bui DCG note itself, to see whether it finds an error only in the W5 step of the 2019 argument or also in the bound's statement. (3) An independent check that the explicit packing algorithm gives uncovered area O(x^{3/5}) for a range of x. (4) Whether McClenagan's thesis and preprint reconcile their statements about the 2019 argument. (5) For the 11-square AI claim (not this bullet's quantity): Ahmed's own announcement, and the repository's README and PROOF.md trust-base statements, to settle the AI attribution.
